SMTO-GIT-0006 — This Git setup uses features SMTO can't check

GUID: b3a515c7-14a4-438f-8c71-ee78c43c2e2e
Slug: git-discovery-unsupported
Domain: GIT · Subsystem: git

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't safely record which Git project was used, because the Git setup on that computer uses something its quick check doesn't support. This doesn't change your Git command's result; SMTO just won't remember the project for later steps.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Keep working, and name the project folder in your requests when you need SMTO to use it. SMTO still runs Git normally; it just can't reuse what it learned about this project between steps.
  2. Open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The exact message names which Git feature stopped the check, such as settings that pull in other settings files.
  3. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to look for include or includeIf lines, a custom core.worktree setting, or Git installed somewhere other than /usr/bin. These are the most common setups SMTO's check can't follow safely, so simplifying them lets SMTO recognize the project.

What success looks like

  • After the next Git command in that folder, this message no longer appears.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't remove Git settings you rely on just to make this message go away; it doesn't block your work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway Git discovery declined to establish repository identity because of an unsupported feature: include/includeIf, custom core.worktree, unsupported config syntax or escapes, an ambiguous GIT_CONFIG_* environment or system config prefix, a non-regular or oversized metadata file, or a filesystem without stable inode identity.

What this means

  • Conservative Git identity discovery encounters unsupported file bounds/identity, escape or config syntax, environment ambiguity, includes, or a worktree route it cannot prove. These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.

Why this can happen

  • Conservative Git identity discovery encounters unsupported file bounds/identity, escape or config syntax, environment ambiguity, includes, or a worktree route it cannot prove.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact unsupported feature and distinguish optimization ineligibility from an ordinary Git command failure.

How to fix it

  • Read the specific message in Technical details (for example 'Included Git configuration requires ordinary discovery'). On the Gateway host, run git config --list --show-origin to find include/includeIf, core.worktree or unusual syntax, and check GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM and that git resolves to /usr/bin/git or /bin/git. Simplify deliberately only if continuity is wanted; SMTO never rewrites Git config or bypasses this check.
  • Use the ordinary supported Git discovery path, or deliberately simplify the identified unsupported configuration. SMTO will not rewrite Git configuration to make an optimization eligible.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported ordinary Git discovery or an unambiguous supported snapshot establishes the intended identity.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
